name: Phalanx Systems GripShadow Infiltration Glove
description:
Street-sourced from a Phalanx Systems secondary label — technically discontinued, practically everywhere in the right circles. Thin-profile neoprene-analog shell with a microsuction gecko-pad palm and finger surface for adhesion on glass, smooth ferrocrete, and lacquered metal. The outer surface is electrostatically neutral, defeating most friction-based print scanners. Interior is smooth enough to prevent secondary print transfer.

Fingers are full-length but the tips are slit with a pull-tab system — fold them back for unmediated touch, snap them forward for full coverage. No branding visible externally. The only identifier is a small embossed triangle inside the left cuff.
functionality: Microsuction palm and fingers provide adhesion on smooth vertical surfaces; electrostatic neutral coat defeats friction-print scanners; pull-tab fingertip system allows rapid switch between full coverage and bare-tip tactile access; no external branding.
what_it_says: You go places you weren't invited and you don't leave evidence.
story_hooks: A security consultant finds GripShadow microsuction residue on a 40th-floor window — whoever made the climb didn't use a rig.
The embossed triangle inside the cuff turns out to be a batch code that traces back to a single production run sold to one buyer three years ago.
A Tier 3 accountant is found wearing a pair — which raises more questions than the missing files ever did.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Gecko Ascender GA-4

physical_description.visual_profile: Form-fitting tactical glove with a sleek, minimal silhouette. Fingers appear slightly bulbous at the tips due to the gecko-pad surface, creating a subtly alien aesthetic. The overall impression is utilitarian and deliberate — designed for function over flash, but with an undeniable edge aesthetic that reads as street-competent and dangerous.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight across the palm and knuckles, conforming closely to hand geometry. Fingers are snug but not restrictive. Cuff sits just below the wrist with enough give for layering under jacket sleeves.
physical_description.primary_material: Neoprene-analog synthetic with microsuction gecko-pad composite on palms and finger surfaces. Electrostatically neutral polymer shell.
physical_description.texture: Outer surface is smooth, almost slick to the eye — designed to be touch-neutral. Palm and finger tips have a distinctive rippled, almost honeycomb microstructure visible under close inspection. Interior is velvet-smooth to minimize friction.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal or deep graphite with subtle iridescent gray undertones that catch light at certain angles. No visible branding or color blocking — pure functional monochrome.
physical_description.closures: None. Friction-fit design that pulls on and off with a slight snap. Pull-tabs at each finger tip allow controlled deployment of the tips.
distinctive_features: Slit finger-tips with pull-tab retraction system for selective touch access
Gecko-pad microsuction surface on palms and digit pads
Electrostatically neutral outer coating defeating print scanners
Small embossed triangle identifier inside left cuff only
Seamless construction with minimal external detailing
Interior smooth finish preventing secondary print transfer
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional — street-accessible but with high-end spec origins. Secondary market Phalanx Systems sourcing signals working-class infiltrator or corpo-adjacent operative.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by urban infiltrators, runners, security specialists, and anyone who climbs ferrocrete or needs tactile precision without leaving traces. Signals technical competence, discretion, and comfort with gray-market hardware. Not street gang — more specialized professional.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly worn. Well-maintained as a tool, not as fashion. May show micro-abrasions on gecko pads from active use, but overall kept in operational condition.
